entry.title: Specification 0.2: RFC 0003 opened for comment, with a window of 23 November 2026 to 8 January 2027 and an issue as the comment ...
entry.content:
23 November 2026.

RFC 0003 opened for comment, with a window of 23 November 2026 to 8 January 2027 and an issue as the comment thread: RFC 0003, a profile defining the five workforce health measures the UK government has named and not defined (work ability, absence, sustained return, retention and disability participation), a minimum group size rule that names the floors already in the privacy profile and sets out how small numbers are withheld or merged, and two proposed record types, CommitmentEvent for the dated commitments and ProviderReturn for a common group-level return from a provider to an employer. The three proposals can be decided separately. Nothing in the core changes until a decision is recorded, and none of it is endorsed by any government department, by BSI or by anyone else.

entry.title: Specification 0.2: Honesty pass item 5 no longer says a richer employer taxonomy would buy resolution at the cost of ...
entry.content:
7 September 2026.

Honesty pass item 5 no longer says a richer employer taxonomy would buy resolution at the cost of comparability. Whether rates are comparable depends on population, collection, numerator and denominator, period and weighting definitions, which neither the schemas nor the category crosswalk establishes.

entry.title: Specification 0.2: The honesty pass argues about the reason taxonomy version 0.2 actually carries.
entry.content:
7 September 2026.

The honesty pass argues about the reason taxonomy version 0.2 actually carries. Version 0.1's six-category enum was replaced by the ten substantive ONS categories and the separate non-disclosure response. The item now distinguishes category alignment from rate comparability: mapping to the ONS categories supports consistent labels, and does not establish that employer episode records and weighted population-survey estimates are comparable.

entry.title: Specification v0.2 draft: Executable schemas for all sixteen entity types (v0.1 had three), with the field tables in the specification ...
entry.content:
6 Sep 2026.

Executable schemas for all sixteen entity types (v0.1 had three), with the field tables in the specification generated from them. The extension mechanism is implemented: namespace syntax, object shape and the recursive named-key restrictions are checked without a profile, and a supplied profile is validated and reported with its version and envelope hash. A checker for a supplied bundle of records applies ten named cross-record rules and reports every finding at a JSON pointer, with a written guide to what it does and does not establish. Privacy classes are carried from v0.1 for the fields that existed there; a nested field without its own class shows its parent's class and says so, and a field with no assignment reads as not separately assigned rather than open. Three code lists are added for the new entity types (the benefit layer, the HSE Management Standards domains and the release category), so the registry holds 27 versioned lists where it held 24; the README and llms.txt say so. The v0.1 draft stays published at its own address. The download is owhs-v0.2-bundle.zip. Corrected in the carried tables: the ReasonableAdjustment end-date anchor said a null meant a standing adjustment; the schema forbids null, so the anchor now says to omit the field when no end date is recorded and to use the status field for adjustment state. The AggregateReport description no longer opens by calling the report the only way individual-level results leave an organisation; it names employer-visible aggregate results and their suppression declarations, with no validation keyword changed.

entry.title: Specification v0.2 schemas, first set: Version 0.2 schemas under schemas/v0.2/; the v0.1 schemas are unchanged at their paths and archived under ...
entry.content:
6 Sep 2026.

Version 0.2 schemas under schemas/v0.2/; the v0.1 schemas are unchanged at their paths and archived under schemas/v0.1/. The three existing entities gain an optional ext object keyed by profile namespace, with the named identifier keys refused at every depth; this is a key-based check, and an identifier inside a permitted string is not detected. WellbeingObservation, InstrumentAdministration, MeasurementContext and AggregateReport become executable schemas, with organisation scope, the context join both measurement entities lacked, occasion timestamps with asserted zones, a closed scoring descriptor and a report period with denominators. The validator adds --profile and rules C3 to C9, and a bundle checker applies the joins between records. absence-reason is 0.2.0: the ten substantive reason categories and the separate non-disclosure response in the ONS 2025 sickness absence workbook, replacing the six-category list that described itself as the ONS taxonomy, with a crosswalk from the legacy codes; org-size-band is 0.1.1, same codes and bounds, with inclusive bounds as metadata and an anchor that no longer calls them a Companies Act classification. The published v0.1 release archive (owhs-v0.1-bundle.zip) is unchanged; the first-set schemas, examples and checkers are in a separate owhs-v0.2-bundle.zip.

entry.title: Specification v0.1: Both RFCs opened for comment, with a window of 7 September to 17 October 2026 and an issue each as the ...
entry.content:
4 Sep 2026.

Both RFCs opened for comment, with a window of 7 September to 17 October 2026 and an issue each as the comment thread: RFC 0001, the construct-domain code list at v0.2, five admissions, two new fields on every code and a mapping from the question bank's topic groups; and RFC 0002, whether a construct about an identified person, such as a manager rated by their team, enters the vocabulary at all, and under what rule. The aggregation floors protect respondents and do nothing for subjects, and RFC 0002 gates RFC 0001: no subject-identifying code is admitted until it is settled.

entry.title: Specification v0.1: Corrections after an external technical review, each one reproduced before it was fixed.
entry.content:
4 Sep 2026.

Corrections after an external technical review, each one reproduced before it was fixed. The reference validator did not assert format, so any string passed where a date was declared; it now asserts every format and refuses to run rather than report a pass it cannot stand behind. An allOf member said end dates must not precede start dates and enforced no ordering; date ordering within a record is now the named rules C1 and C2 at Level 1, implemented in the validator, because JSON Schema cannot compare two fields of an instance. A direct-identifier member duplicated additionalProperties: false and claimed to forbid identifiers "anywhere", which was untrue of values; the privacy profile now separates what is enforced from what is a producer obligation. value on AggregateReport was unconditionally required while section 9 required a producer below a floor to suppress and not emit it, so no conformant suppressed report could exist; corrected with an erratum. Level 3 now states that no tool in the repository verifies it, and why parts of it cannot be verified from a payload at all. Full detail in CHANGELOG.md.
